data.exact_reserve_text: The profit on the technical account of GBP 38.2m (2014 restated: profit GBP 62.3m) includes a run-off surplus of GBP 16.4m for prior accident years (2014: GBP 5.2m surplus). This included a surplus of GBP 5.8m for reinsurance acceptance business and a surplus of GBP 10.6m on direct business (2014: surplus of GBP 13.4m for reinsurance acceptance business and a deficit of GBP 8.2m on direct business).
data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate recorded a net prior-accident-year run-off release. Based on the gross claims development triangle, older underwriting years (notably 2011-2013) produced a combined favourable development of approximately GBP 13.75m (release), representing about a 3.1% reduction versus opening gross claims outstanding. The managing agent also reports a run-off surplus for prior accident years (quoted as GBP 16.4m) with reported components for reinsurance acceptances and direct business; the gross triangle-derived figure has been used for the gross PY movement.
raw_causal_phrases: run-off surplus of GBP 16.4m for prior accident years (2014: GBP 5.2m surplus)

This included a surplus of GBP 5.8m for reinsurance acceptance business and a surplus of GBP 10.6m on direct business (2014: surplus of GBP 13.4m for reinsurance acceptance business and a deficit of GBP 8.2m on direct business)
data.data_quality_notes: The gross prior-year movement has been calculated from the published gross claims development triangle (gross figures, GBP '000s). The managing agent narrative quotes a 'run-off surplus of GBP 16.4m' for prior accident years and component amounts for reinsurance acceptance and direct business; that narrative figure appears to be a different measure (likely net of reinsurance or covering a slightly different set of years) and therefore the triangle-derived gross figure (-GBP 13.749m) has been used for the primary prior_year_development_gbp_m. Confidence levels reflect this: triangle-based total = 0.8; narrative split figures used for LOB breakdown are lower confidence (0.5).
